cases.reason: The contract places the Export CSV button above the shop admin’s Orders table and gives reviewers concrete checks for the download, one row per displayed order, the four columns in order, and the date filter.
The contract identifies the Quillmoor members site, specifies a 30-minute lifetime for password reset links, and gives testable outcomes for links opened before and after expiry.
The contract specifies a print stylesheet for Larkspur Kitchen’s recipe pages, identifies what to keep and hide, and provides a checkable one-page A4 PDF test using the Barley Soup recipe.
The contract names the script and log path, specifies what each entry must contain, and gives checkable criteria for successful backups and archive write failures.
The task specifies that Hollowbrook’s guest invitations must show the event’s stored time zone abbreviation after the start time, and the Berlin and New York examples make the result checkable.

The goal specifies what the Driftwood help centre’s search results page should show when no articles match, and searching for zzqqxx lets a reviewer verify the message, contact form link, and search box position.

The goal names the two headers and the public forecast API, the details identify API callers and the existing hourly limit, and the criteria let a reviewer verify the limit and the one-call decrease in the remaining count.
The contract names the guide’s repository path and audience, specifies the access and tool information it must include, and gives reviewers concrete checks for its contents and printed length.
The goal identifies the Thimblevane shop’s About page and the exact heading change, and the first criterion lets a reviewer verify that the heading reads “Our story.”

The task specifies raising the Quillmoor members site’s idle timeout from 15 to 60 minutes for members reading long articles and gives a checkable criterion that a member stays signed in after 45 minutes of inactivity.
The contract identifies the map image on the Larkspur Kitchen blog’s Contact page, names screen reader users as the audience, and gives the exact alt text a reviewer can verify.
The goal identifies the Hollowbrook RSVP form, the button to rename, and the purpose for guests, and the first criterion lets a reviewer verify that the button reads “Send my reply.”
The task identifies the Driftwood help centre but leaves the change unspecified and gives the independent reviewer no concrete improvement to verify.
The contract leaves unspecified which parts of the Thimblevane shop need updating and what a reviewer should check to confirm completion.
The contract identifies the app and report users and requires every report to open without errors, but it never specifies what work to do on the reports.
The contract identifies the Quillmoor sign-up flow and checks that new members can still register, but leaves the intended change unspecified.

The goal identifies the page and photo change, and the details identify the audience, but none of the acceptance criteria says what a reviewer can verify to determine whether the redesign is complete.
The criteria rely on perceived speed, staff happiness, and reviewer agreement without specifying how to verify any of them.
The goal identifies the Hollowbrook RSVP form and its guests, but the criteria give the reviewer no specific feature or outcome to verify.
The acceptance criteria rely on subjective judgments and unspecified approval, so they give a reviewer no concrete check for the newsletter sign-up box.
The contract names the Fernhollow weather app but leaves the intended change undefined and gives the reviewer no observable condition to check.
The goal names the Tallowmere codebase but specifies no concrete change, and neither criterion defines an observable result.
The goal names the Quillmoor members site but leaves the work undefined, and neither criterion identifies a specific result or behavior to verify.
The contract names the Thimblevane shop but leaves the monthly changes unspecified and gives reviewers no observable completion criterion.
